content.doc_md:
The History API is accessed with thewindow.historyobject. Thehistoryobject can be written without the window prefix. Common metods are: Thehistory.back()method loads the previous page in the session history. This is the same as clicking the browser's Back button. Thehistory.back()method is equivalent tohistory.go(-1). Thehistory.forward()method loads the next page in the session history. This is the same as clicking the browser's Forward button. Theforward()method is equivalent tohistory.go(1). Thehistory.go()method loads a specific page from the session history. The argument tells the browser how many steps to move from the current page. Thehistory.lengthproperty returns the number of entries in the session history. The current page is included in the number. Thehistory.stateproperty returns the state data associated with the current history entry. The History API can also add or replace entries in the browser history. This is useful for applications that change page content without loading a completely new document. The two methods are: Thehistory.pushState()method adds a new entry to the session history. The example changes the URL topage2.htmland adds a new history entry. It does not loadpage2.htmlfrom the server. Astateobject can store any data associated with the history entry. The second argument exists for historical reasons and is normally an empty string. The optionalurlmust have the same origin as the current page. history.state isnulluntil you call history.pushState() or history.replaceState(). Thehistory.replaceState()method changes the current history entry. UnlikepushState(), it does not create a new history entry. This changes the current URL without adding another entry to the browser history. Thepopstateevent occurs when the active history entry changes. This normally happens when the user clicks the browser's Back or Forward button. If a history entry contains state data, it is available fromevent.state: The following example changes the URL without loading a new page. It also restores the displayed content when the user clicks Back or Forward. Browsers normally restore the scroll position when users move backward or forward. Thehistory.scrollRestorationproperty can control this behavior. The possible values are: Useback(),forward(), andgo()to navigate through the session history. UsepushState()to create a new history entry without loading a new page. UsereplaceState()to change the current history entry. Use thepopstateevent to detect when the user moves to another history entry. ### Code Snippets ``` let length = window.history.length; --- let length = history.length; --- --- --- --- --- let length = history.length; --- let state = history.state; --- let state = {name:"example", page: 2}; let url = "page2.html"; history.pushState(state, "", url); --- history.pushState(state, "", url) --- history.replaceState(null, "", "newpage.html"); --- history.replaceState(state, "", url) --- window.addEventListener("popstate", function(event) { document.getElementById("demo").innerHTML = "Page changed"; }); --- window.addEventListener("popstate", function(event) { if (event.state) { document.getElementById("demo").innerHTML = event.state.page; } }); ---

Home

--- history.scrollRestoration = "manual"; ```
